title: Stanford's AI Curriculum
source: Mann's picks — the order Stanford's own AI courses assume, not a department's requirements
blurb: Three prerequisites, a two-course core, and the specializations that open up after it. Every step has lecture video online.

steps.note: Probability written for programmers. CS229's first two weeks assume all of it.
The linear algebra slot. Stanford points people at Math 51 or CS205L here, and neither is online — Boyd's ENGR108 covers the same ground and is.
The one you can defer. Skip it and CS229's optimization sections stay a black box you trust rather than read.
The trunk of the whole thing. Ng's 2018 run is the one people mean when they say CS229.
Deep learning after CS229's classical ML. Same lecturer, and it assumes you sat through the earlier course.
Vision. The 2017 run is the famous one, but take a recent year if you want transformers in it.
NLP, and in practice the fastest route to understanding how language models are put together.
Reinforcement learning. The least like the other three — closer to control theory than to the rest of this map.
Graphs. Leskovec's Winter 2021 run is complete and the one to take.
Generative models — diffusion, VAEs, autoregressive models — from the vision side of the map.
Build a language model end to end. The heaviest course here and the one that assumes the most.
Meta-learning and multi-task learning. Finn's course, and it leans on the RL material.
